note: Rewritten from entry 28 (pp. 123–128) of Roonwal and Maiti (1966) "Termites from Indonesia including West Irian" (Treubia 27(1): 63–140), the original in English; the original is the original description (n. sp.), with only the soldier and the major and minor workers, the alate being recorded as "Unknown". The "4. WORKER MINOR" heading on the first page of the original is in fact the start of the soldier section (the text that follows treats the nasus and the frontal gland duct) and has been placed in the soldier section by content. The measurement tables of the original (Tables 9–10), figure numbers, type specimens and geographical distribution have not been entered item by item; the figures are taken from the text and the tables. Doubtful OCR readings (e.g. "18 segments" should be 13, "0.98—0.98") have been read following the sense of the table, and what could not be determined has not been entered.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule pyriform, constricted behind the antennae (minimum width 0.42—0.50 mm), 0.96—1.00 mm long without the rostrum, maximum width 0.78—0.85 mm; rostrum subcylindrical, slender, 0.48—0.55 mm long, about half the head length; antennae 13—14-segmented; postmentum nearly hexagonal, 0.27—0.31 mm long, 0.27—0.32 mm wide; pronotum saddle-shaped, 0.44—0.48 mm wide, 0.15—0.20 mm long; body length about 3.5—3.7 mm. Major worker with 15-segmented antennae, minor worker with 14; the pronotum of the minor worker is only weakly saddle-shaped. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish brown, paler posteriorly; apex of the rostrum darker; antennae pale brown; legs yellowish white; thoracic tergites pale yellow; abdominal tergites brown, the sternites paler. Vertex with 1 pair of hairs; apex of the rostrum with hairs. Body length excluding antennae, including the rostrum, about 3.5—3.7 mm. Head capsule pyriform, constricted behind the antennae (minimum width 0.42—0.50 mm); longer than wide (head length without the rostrum 0.96—1.00 mm, maximum width 0.78—0.85 mm); widest posteriorly, posterior margin rounded; dorsal outline weakly concave. Rostrum subcylindrical, slender, gradually narrowing to a narrow, weakly pointed apex; about half the head length (0.48—0.55 mm); basal swelling indistinct. Frontal gland duct visible within the rostrum, the frontal gland distinct. Compound eyes and ocelli absent. Antennae usually 13-segmented, sometimes 14; segment 1 long, cylindrical; segment 2 about half of segment 3 (in the 14-segmented condition nearly as long as segment 3); segment 4 smaller than segment 3; segments 5—8 gradually longer and clavate; segment 9 to the penultimate subequal, clavate; terminal segment narrower. Anteclypeus a thin, white, transparent narrow band along the anterior margin of the postclypeus; postclypeus nearly rectangular, brown, transversely arched, separated from the body by an indistinct groove. Labrum nearly rectangular, anterior and lateral margins weakly convex. Mandibles small, reduced; apical process distinct, its outer margin almost straight and its base wide; the apical process with 1 minute tooth (its position on the left mandible, the right mandible or both varies); molar plate straight or weakly convex. Postmentum nearly hexagonal, with a few setae near the anterior margin; slightly wider than long (median length 0.27—0.31 mm, maximum width 0.27—0.32 mm); widest almost at the middle, the sides narrowing gradually forwards and backwards; anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin concave. Pronotum saddle-shaped, microscopically hairy, much narrower than the head (maximum width 0.44—0.48 mm, length 0.15—0.20 mm); sides narrowing posteriorly; anterior margin convex with a weak median depression; posterior margin convex with a median notch. Mesonotum narrower than the pronotum; metanotum nearly equal to the pronotum. Legs slender, rather long, hairy; hind femora not reaching the end of the abdomen; tibial apical spur formula 2:2:2; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate, hairy, each tergite with a few microscopic hairs, tergites of the posterior 3—4 segments with long hairs, the sternites more densely hairy than the tergites; cerci short, 2-segmented; styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: head pale brown; mandibles yellowish brown with dark brown tooth margins; thorax and abdomen milky white. Head and body moderately hairy. Body length excluding antennae about 4.0—4.8 mm. Head capsule square, length nearly equal to width (length to the mandibular base 0.98—1.10 mm, maximum width 1.00—1.16 mm); posterior margin broadly rounded; Y-shaped suture distinct; frontal gland at the junction of the Y-shaped suture in the middle of the vertex, covered by a translucent oval plate. Compound eyes and ocelli absent. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 1 longest; segment 2 nearly half of segment 1; segment 3 smallest; segment 4 slightly smaller than segment 2 and nearly as long as segment 5; segments 6—9 gradually longer and pyriform; segments 10—14 subequal; terminal segment slightly narrower than segment 14. Anteclypeus transparent, white, hairless, its anterior margin projecting forwards in the middle; postclypeus arched, hairy, divided into equal halves by a median suture. Labrum slightly wider than long, widest in the middle, anterior end weakly concave and hairy. Mandibles of the typical Bulbitermes type: left mandible with 1 apical and 2 marginal teeth, the apical tooth conical and sharp; the first marginal tooth blunter, close to the apical tooth and nearly as large; the second marginal tooth smallest, far from the first. Right mandible also with 1 apical and 2 marginal teeth, the apical tooth pointed at the apex, slightly smaller than or nearly equal to the first marginal tooth; the first marginal tooth stout and sharp; the second marginal tooth blunt, smallest, close to the first. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, wider than long (maximum width 0.60—0.66 mm, maximum length 0.28—0.33 mm); sides narrowing posteriorly; anterior margin with more hairs, convex, with a very weak median notch; posterior margin nearly straight, without a notch. Legs short, slender, hairy; hind femora not reaching the end of the abdomen; tibial apical spur formula 2:2:2; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen long, hairy, the sternites more densely hairy than the tergites; cerci 2-segmented; styli absent. Minor worker similar to the major worker but differing as follows: body smaller (about 3.5—3.8 mm versus 4.0—4.8 mm); antennae 14-segmented (versus 15); antennal segment 3 smaller than segment 2 and segment 4 smallest (in the major worker segment 3 is smallest and segment 4 slightly smaller than segment 2); pronotum weakly saddle-shaped (versus strongly saddle-shaped).
